To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have characterized the variation in lipid profiles and sensory parameters and represented the diversity among 16 cattle populations, which is of interest for the beef industry.

the correlations between fat content, sensory parameters and lipid profile in cattle meat are complex, and that the variation in the lipid profile and sensory characteristics of meat is mainly due to genetic factors.

the variation in fatty acid profiles and sensory parameters is influenced by both phenotypic and genetic factors and that these factors can be used for a better characterization of the diversity of cattle populations and the development of low-density SNP chips for meat quality traits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the variation of lipid profiles and sensory parameters among 15 cattle breeds and their genetic basis.
providing information that will be useful to breeders and consumers, as well as to the food industry.
the development of a better understanding of the genetic and phenotypic background of beef meat, in order to help the beef sector to meet the demands of a changing society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a moderate fatness score is associated with a higher content of PUFA in beef, which is related to better flavour scores.
the breed, the fatness score, the FA profile and the sensory parameters are all interrelated.
the variation in FA profile is a consequence of the breed, and the variation in sensory traits is the consequence of breed and the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the variation of FA profile is mainly driven by the breed effect and that the breed effect is more important than the genotype effect.
the variation in the FA profile of bovine meat is a consequence of a complex interaction of genetic, environmental and nutritional factors.
the use of low-density panels of SNPs with predictive value for meat quality traits may be a useful tool for the selection of animals with desirable characteristics in the beef industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the high genetic variation in FA composition and organoleptic traits, there is a strong phenotypic and genetic correlation between them.

the genetic background is an important determinant of the variation in FA composition and organoleptic characteristics in cattle, which is reflected in the different phenotypic and genetic distances between the breeds.

, in the case of beef, the breed effect is the most important factor influencing the FA profile and sensory characteristics, which should be considered in the design of breeding strategies for the improvement of meat quality traits.
